newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN CALL UP AT CLOSE IN STRAY DEALS, GILTS FLAT.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN CALL UP AT CLOSE IN STRAY DEALS, GILTS FLAT.

text.p: Indian call money rose briefly in stray deals just before close Thursday, after range-bound trade most of the day, dealers said.
They said good liquidity with the system kept most of the day's trade between 3.25 and 3.75 percent but rates touched 4.5 percent just before close when some lenders went off the market.
"Some big lenders were absent just before close," said a public sector bank dealer.
"There were a couple of banks with some borrowing requirements. This pushed up rates up to 4.5 percent briefly but these were stray deals," he said.
Call money closed Wednesday at 3.5-4.0 percent.
Dealers said prices of governemnt securities were almost flat in quiet trade as market players took a breather ahead of a 30-billion rupee bond auction on Monday.
"Trade will pick up only after the auction results are out," said a dealer. "We will then be able to take a view on liquidity and the yield curve."
Among actively-traded stocks, the 12.59 percent 2004 traded between 106.28 and 106.32 rupees against Wednesday's close of 106.30.
The 12.69 percent 2002 and 13.05 percent 2007 traded unchanged at 106.30 and 109 respectively.
Treasury bills maturing on July 18, 1998 yielded 8.05 percent against 7.93.
